subject: human voice and vocal folds
title: What If You Never Stopped Talking?

scenes.text: What if you never stopped talking? Two tiny folds in your throat would give up first.
Every time you speak, your vocal folds slap together, up to about two hundred times a second.
One hour of nonstop speech means about seven hundred thousand collisions. Most of us voice only about a tenth of each hour.
Teachers voice nearly a quarter of their working day, and about forty percent say they've lost their voice at some point.
Researchers suspect silences of several minutes let the folds recover. Nonstop talking means those pauses never come.
So your words would never run out. Your voice would, and the only fix is the one thing you refused to do.

description:
What if you never stopped talking? At an average pitch of about 200 Hz, vocal folds collide about 200 times a second, roughly 720,000 times per hour of continuous voicing, according to voice scientist Ingo Titze.
Teachers voice nearly a quarter of their working time, and about 40% report losing their voice at some point in their careers; breaks of several minutes may help the folds recover.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: Your vocal folds have hit each other thousands of times today already. What body habit should we run through next?
